attempted_claim: Let Gamma be the set of growth rates gr(C)=lim_{n->infty} |C_n|^{1/n} of proper permutation classes where the limit exists, let lambda=inf{gamma : (gamma,infinity) subset Gamma}, and let lambda_B approx 2.35698 be the unique positive root of x^8-2x^7-x^5-x^4-2x^3-2x^2-x-1. Is lambda=lambda_B?
decisive_failure: No universal gap theorem for arbitrary permutation classes near growth 2.35 was available, since grid and simple-permutation classifications break down above kappa approx 2.20557; finite-profile computation provably cannot separate true gaps from description-complexity artifacts, so neither sharpness nor disproof of lambda=lambda_B could be advanced within the pass.
